mentions.sentence: Moreover, others [ 32,36,41] support complex SQL operations and predicates but lacks guidance for avoiding redundant or ineffective workloads.
mentions.context_before: ineffective workloads. The redundant workloads are characterized by repeating a similar partial order of record accesses, while the ineffective workloads appear when the expected conflict cannot be formed due to unreasonable scheduling (e.g., the record expected to be accessed by an operation is deleted by another parallel operation, and then it could not access its expected record or participate in any conflict formation). Some of existing work [ 3,16,66] has been designed to only generate simplified key-value operations, and they might omit some bugs triggered by more complex SQL operations.
mentions.context_after: Anomaly-sensitive Testing (C3). DBMSs have various ILs, each with a distinctive definition to preclude specific non-serializable anomalies [ 13,22,27,64]. Although the effective testing could provide various scenarios for IL test, it could not help customize some specific non-serializable anomalies. Then, to effectively test various ILs, it imposes the requirement of generating anomaly-sensitive workloads which check whether an IL prohibits the anomalies as defined. However, customizing non-serializable anomalies is still vacant in existing researches [19, 24, 32, 33, 36, 39, 43, 53, 57, 77].

analysis.summary: DBStorm generates workloads for testing isolation-level implementations. Its argument is that query-oriented tools only exercise the query engine, while existing transaction-oriented tools execute a few operations serially and so build sparse conflict graphs that never contain a cycle. DBStorm instead constructs workloads targeting chosen non-serializable anomalies, using conflict-graph isomorphism to avoid generating redundant ones. It found 20 isolation bugs and 13 others.
analysis.narrative: SQLancer supplies DBStorm's SQL. The paper states that because SQLancer targets the relational model it is used to generate syntactically and semantically correct SQL operations, and that since SQLancer mainly produces serially executed operations they revised it to generate parallel ones. It is also one of the tools measured against, and the comparison makes the paper's point precisely: SQLsmith, SQLancer and Squirrel between them reveal 760 bugs of which none is an isolation bug, because they execute transactions sequentially in a single thread and so cannot produce a cycle in the conflict graph at all.
